newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court sets Socialist funding verdict May 29.
newsitem.headline: French court sets Socialist funding verdict May 29.

text.p: LYON, France (March 25) Reuter - A French court said on Tuesday it would pass judgement on May 29 in the trial of senior opposition Socialist politicians accused of running an illicit party funding scheme.

The public prosecutor is seeking suspended prison terms and electoral bans against Henri Emmanuelli and Andre Laignel, two former Socialist party treasurers. Emmanuelli, a member of parliament and ex-minister, served as party leader in 1994-95.
The prosecutor also called for 18-month suspended sentences against two former parliamentarians, Michel Pezet and Philippe Sanmarco, and a two-year bar on their standing for election.
Defence lawyers pleaded for acquittal on Tuesday, saying their clients had sought political donations and not peddled their influence.
Since there were no laws covering political financing at the time, the defendants could not be convicted of a crime, they said.
"This happened in a legal vacuum," said Laignel's lawyer Olivier Metzner. "This is the only party that had the courage to admit having a parallel financing channel."

Emmanuelli and Laignel told the court they took political reponsibility for schemes to funnel money to the party in the late 1980s via the Urba consultancy firm but said they had not profited personally and maintained they had not broken any laws.

All France's mainstream parties ran covert funding schemes before a 1990 law put political finances on a legal footing. Magistrates are investigating similar cases involving the ruling centre-right RPR and UDF parties and the Communist party.
Emmanuelli was party treasurer from 1988 to 1991 while Laignel held the post from 1981 to 1988.

Emmanuelli has already been convicted on similar charges in a 1995 trial in Brittany. He was given a one-year suspended jail term and 30,000 franc fine for receiving illicit campaign funds from the front company run by party insiders.
In the current case, Emmanuelli was charged with handling stolen goods and influence peddling. Laignel was on trial for being an accomplice to the same offences.
Investigators uncovered a covert funding network used by the Socialists to finance their campaigns by taking rake-offs from public works contracts through companies such as Urba.
The front companies solicited fees from firms seeking public tenders. Part of the money was funnelled to local Socialist candidates and the national party.

The second trial was based on similar accusations involving Urba in the Mediterranean port city of Marseille. Prosecutors say the party illegally skimmed 9.4 million francs from public works contracts awarded in the region in 1988 and 1989.
